pr.title: coverage: `llvm-cov` expects column numbers to be bytes, not code points
pr.description:
Normally the compiler emits column numbers as a 1-based number of Unicode code points.

But when we embed coverage mappings for `-Cinstrument-coverage`, those mappings will ultimately be read by the `llvm-cov` tool. That tool assumes that column numbers are 1-based numbers of *bytes*, and relies on that assumption when slicing up source code to apply highlighting (in HTML reports, and in text-based reports with colour).

For the very common case of all-ASCII source code, bytes and code points are the same, so the difference isn't noticeable. But for code that contains non-ASCII characters, emitting column numbers as code points will result in `llvm-cov` slicing strings in the wrong places, producing mangled output or fatal errors.

(See https://github.com/taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov/issues/275 as an example of what can go wrong.)
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.summary: InstrumentCoverage must emit coverage-map column numbers as 1-based UTF-8 byte offsets, not Unicode code points, because llvm-cov slices source by bytes. Using code-point columns mangles non-ASCII source or makes llvm-cov fail; empty spans must also be expanded by whole UTF-8 character byte lengths at char boundaries.
analysis.originalLogic: Coverage mapping construction in `make_code_region` converted a `Span` to coordinates via the general-purpose `source_map.span_to_location_info(span)`, whose columns are 1-based counts of Unicode code points. Empty spans were widened by one column with `start_col = start_col.saturating_sub(1)` or `end_col = start_col + 1`. The resulting `CodeRegion { start_col, end_col }` was embedded in the function's coverage map for `llvm-cov`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, the pass emitted code-point-indexed columns in coverage mappings (`-Cinstrument-coverage`) instead of byte-indexed columns. On lines containing multi-byte UTF-8 before a mapped span, start/end columns were too small for `llvm-cov`, which assumes column numbers are 1-based numbers of bytes and relies on that assumption when slicing source. Additionally, empty spans were expanded by one code-point column rather than by the byte width of the adjacent character, so expansion could land inside a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence. The fix replaces `span_to_location_info` with `file.relative_position`/`lookup_line` byte-column computation and expands empty spans with `src.ceil_char_boundary(hi_rpos + 1) - hi_rpos` or `lo_rpos - src.floor_char_boundary(lo_rpos - 1)`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust source compiled with coverage instrumentation where mapped spans occur on lines containing non-ASCII characters (multi-byte UTF-8) before or within the span, e.g. Unicode identifiers, string contents, or macro-generated code. ASCII-only source is in the domain too but does not distinguish the two transformations because bytes equal code points there.
analysis.trigger: A coverage-relevant span starts after one or more multi-byte UTF-8 characters on the same line, so byte offset and code-point offset differ; and/or an empty coverage span is adjacent to a multi-byte character and gets widened.
preconditions: The crate/function is being compiled with `-Cinstrument-coverage` so coverage mappings are emitted.
The source line of a mapped span contains non-ASCII UTF-8 before the span start or inside the mapped region.
The generated coverage map is consumed by LLVM `llvm-cov` (e.g. report/HTML/text output that slices source by byte columns).
For empty-span expansion: the span is empty, lies within the body span, and the source file text is available.
pitfalls: Testing only ASCII source cannot expose the difference because bytes and code points coincide there.
Column expansion for empty spans must use char-boundary-aware byte nudges; blindly adding 1 or subtracting 1 can split a multi-byte UTF-8 character.
Empty spans at end of line: resolve line/column before nudging so the extra column does not wrap to the next line.
Doctest line offsets are applied but FYI there is no way to offset doctest columns (`FIXME(#79417)`).

Spans crossing multiple files or failing coordinate lookup should be skipped (`make_code_region` returns `Option`), and a function with no valid mappings is skipped rather than causing an ICE or user-unavoidable llvm-cov failure.
Column numbers remain 1-based; the change is units (bytes), not base.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a coverage UI test with non-ASCII identifiers, string contents, and macro-defined functions, compiled with `-Cinstrument-coverage` and `--use-color` for llvm-cov. Assert exact `.cov-map` mappings whose columns are byte offsets (e.g. `サビ` mapping columns 20..24 and `他` columns 25..37), confirming a code-point implementation would produce smaller columns. Also assert a `.coverage` report shows valid llvm-cov slicing/highlighting of the multi-byte lines rather than mangled UTF-8. Compare only the coverage mapping values, not irrelevant MIR; include an ASCII-only case as a control that should be unchanged. Do not claim llvm-cov was executed; this corpus only inspects the historical regression expectations.
